images.title: Writing a number from its name
images.purpose: Show a number name on a ticket, its parts matched to the chart places, and the number written from them.
images.composition: A ticket with the name on top, a one-row chart in the middle joined to the ticket parts by arrows, and the number below.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Top: a ticket, a wide rounded rectangle about 1150 by 130 px with a small semicircular notch cut in the middle of its left end and of its right end, a thin dark outline and a white fill. On it the one line Sixty-eight thousand five hundred nineteen in dark text (50 px), with 3 pale highlight bands behind the words: Sixty-eight thousand on a pale blue band (tint of #0072B2), five hundred on a pale amber band (tint of #E69F00), nineteen on a pale reddish purple band (tint of #CC79A7). Middle: a chart of 5 columns about 210 px wide and 2 rows. Header row: TTh, Th, H, T, O in white bold letters on blue #0072B2 cells. Digit row: 6, 8, 5, 1, 9 in large bold dark numerals (90 px), with the cells tinted to match the ticket: 6 and 8 pale blue, 5 pale amber, 1 and 9 pale reddish purple. 3 thin dark arrows run from the 3 bands down to their cells: from the blue band to the TTh and Th cells, from the amber band to the H cell, from the purple band to the T and O cells. Bottom: the number 68,519 in very large bold dark numerals (120 px) with the comma clear.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Write the digits you hear from the left, put each in its own place, and put the comma before the last three digits.
images.description: A ticket reading Sixty-eight thousand five hundred nineteen with colour bands matched by arrows to the chart digits 6, 8, 5, 1, 9, and the number 68,519 below.
images.context: Concept image for Writing a number from its name. It follows the ticket, chart and digits idea of the figure in your maths book and uses the video's own example, 68,519.
images.teaching_notes: Have students find the word thousand first. The part before it fills TTh and Th, and the part after it fills H, T and O. The colours only group the parts; every digit is also written.

image_decisions.why: A ticket matched to the chart places shows how the words of a number name become digits.
